newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai interbank rate rises, baht lower near close.
newsitem.headline: Thai interbank rate rises, baht lower near close.

text.p: Tightened liquidity pushed the Thai overnight interbank rate up further to 11.00-11.50 percent late on Monday from 10.50-11.00 in the morning and 9.25-9.50 on Friday, dealers said.
Dealers attributed the higher rate to demand for baht funds used by dealers to buy dollars and by banks building their reserves to meet the next deadline on December 7.
"Some foreign banks here are short on baht and they come in as bidders in the interbank market which further tighten liquidity," a dealer at Bangkok Bank said.
The baht eased to 25.453-25.458 to the dollar during late trade from 25.443-25.446 in the morning and 24.414-25.417 late on Friday on a stronger dollar in major markets, dealers said.
"The dollar is still on an upward trend (against yen and mark) which boosts demand for the greenback," a dealer at Thai Farmers Bank said.
Dealers said the dollar rally was not related to a current clouded domestic market outlook caused by a delay by coalition leader Chavalit Yongchaiyudh in forming his cabinet.
The one-month dollar/baht swap premium also rose further to 10.10/11.10 satangs per dollar late on Monday from 9.50/10.50 early in the morning and 9.00/10.00 late on Friday.
The Bank of Thailand fixed the dollar/baht mid-rate at 25.43 against 25.40 on Friday.
